Hi Alicia — thanks for the context and the usage file.

Short answer: yes, we can structure a multi-year prepay that locks your unit pricing for the contract term. There are a few levers we typically use to balance value for both sides:
- Term length discounts: 1Y (baseline), 2Y (5–8% discount), 3Y+ (10–15% discount depending on commit size)
- Annual ramp schedule: fixed annual minimums with the ability to pre-pay for full amount (e.g., Year1 60%, Year2 80%, Year3 100%) or step-up billing to align with expected growth
- Price cap vs price freeze: we can offer a hard freeze for committed units, and a capped increase for overages (typically index-linked)

I'll draft two concrete proposals: a straight 3-year prepay with a 12% term discount and a 2+1 structure where you prepay Years 1–2 and have a renewable option for Year 3 with slightly higher discount.

Looping in Rishi for finance/pricing confirmation and Laura for approvals on escalated terms (SLA and invoicing cadence).

Are you able to share the expected growth curve (conservative, baseline, aggressive) for the next 36 months? That will help pick the right ramp.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole

I'll provision a formal quote and include an amendment template for your legal team. Recommend the 3-year freeze for customers where predictability is critical — it simplifies cost modeling for procurement.

Option A (Annual renew): Standard 1Y renewal, no price lock, discounted gross-rate 3% for annual prepay

Carlos — appreciate the questions; recap and proposed commitments below.

Recap: FinexCo wants a 3-year prepay to lock net pricing while preserving flexibility for material business change.

Redwood proposed commitments:
- Refund/credit: pro rata refunds available only in the case of enterprise-level decommissioning or divestiture (M&A) with 60 days notice; standard churn does not qualify for refunding but unused credits can bank up to 12 months and applied to other Redwood products
- New units: for the term we will extend the frozen unit price to incremental purchases up to 20% annual growth over committed baseline. Above 20% growth, incremental units billed at the committed unit price + overage uplift (TBD; proposed 8%)
- Early termination: if FinexCo terminates for convenience, remaining prepaid amounts are non-refundable unless M&A clause triggers (as above)

Next steps I propose:
1) We accept a limited M&A refund clause as drafted above.
2) Redwood legal will incorporate the 20% annual ramp extension and 8% overage uplift into the amendment; we will share a redline by EOD tomorrow.
3) Procurement signs off and Finance issues full invoice on the selected prepay cadence.

If that aligns, we'll draft final redline and route for signatures.

Thanks — happy to call if you want to walk through the SOW/ramp math.

-Marissa
